vault.duplicate_hint: Merging keeps one entry on this device. All connections stay: they are stored in the vault itself, and nothing changes for anyone else.
settings.title: Settings
settings.x11_desc: Shows windows of programs you start on a server (X11 forwarding). Turning it on downloads VcXsrv, about 49 MB, once.
settings.x11_installed: VcXsrv {{version}} is ready. Sessions with ForwardX11 show their windows here. Turn off to remove it.
settings.x11_system: This system's own X server is used for X11 forwarding.
settings.x11_mac: X11 forwarding on a Mac needs XQuartz (xquartz.org).
settings.x11_failed: The X11 server could not be set up: {{error}}
themes.error: Could not reach the theme registry
settings.paste_warning_desc: A pasted newline runs the command as soon as it arrives. Ask first, so a stray copy cannot execute on a server before you have read it.
settings.paste_threshold_desc: Pastes with fewer lines than this go straight to the terminal.
settings.shell_colors: Type a colour setup into the shell
settings.shell_colors_desc: Off by default. Servers colour their own prompt and ls for Reach's xterm-256color terminal, as they do for PuTTY. When on, Reach types a short colour and prompt setup after login; it keeps it out of bash and zsh history, but a few shells (BusyBox, some zsh setups) may still record it.
settings.rdp_hw_render_desc: Paint the desktop through the GPU. Applies to desktops opened after the change.
settings.rdp_gfx_desc: Ask the host for the graphics pipeline, which carries video as H.264 on hosts that encode it. On a host that does not, the picture gets heavier, not lighter.
settings.shell_desc: Shell used when opening new local terminals
settings.restore_tabs_desc: Restore tabs from previous session on startup
settings.tray_desc: Keep running in system tray when window is closed
settings.community_desc: Chat, support and release announcements on Discord.
report.title: Report a problem
report.desc: Opens a GitHub issue with Reach's log to attach, cleaned of your hosts, accounts and folders.
report.cleaned: This is the log as it will be shared. Your hosts, user names, session names, IP addresses and home folder were replaced. Read it, and remove anything else you would rather keep private.
report.partial: Saved sessions could not be read, so their hosts and names may still be in this log. Read it before you attach it.
report.after: The issue is open in your browser. Describe what happened, then drag reach-report.log from the folder that just opened into the issue.
settings.support_desc: Reach is free and built on no budget. Sponsoring is what would pay for a signing certificate, a test server, and the time to build more.
community.title: Join the Reach community
community.body: There is a Discord for Reach. Ask questions, hear about new versions, or help decide where it goes next.
community.point_help: Help with connections, sync and builds
community.point_releases: New versions announced as they ship
settings.system_startup_desc: Launch Reach automatically when you log in
settings.font_desc: Font used in the terminal emulator

sharing.title: Session sharing
sharing.start_desc: You make a code and send it to them.
sharing.join_desc: You paste the code they sent you.
sharing.read_write_warn: They will be able to type into your terminal as you. Enforced on this machine; you can switch it back at any time.
sharing.preparing: Finding a route… this takes a few seconds.
sharing.waiting: Waiting for them to connect. This closes on its own once they do.
sharing.fail_no_path: No route between the two machines. This is almost always a NAT that blocks direct connections. It works if both of you are on the same network or VPN, or with a TURN server added under Settings → Sharing.
sharing.fail_bad_code: That code is not for this share. Check it was copied completely.
sharing.fail_tampered: A message arrived that could not be verified, so the connection was closed.
sharing.fail_timeout: The other side did not connect in time.
sharing.remote_view_only: View only. They have not allowed typing.
sharing.enable_desc: Share a terminal with another person, peer to peer, encrypted end to end. Off by default. While it is off none of this code is loaded, and while it is on nothing connects until you click Share.
sharing.ice_desc: Used only when you click Share, and only to find a route to the other machine. Your list, in your order.
sharing.ice_empty: No servers. Sharing will work only on the same network.
sharing.stun_note: STUN only answers "what is my public address?". It carries none of your traffic, costs nothing to run, and the defaults are public servers run by Google and Cloudflare.
sharing.turn_note: TURN relays your traffic when a direct route cannot be found. There is no free public TURN worth trusting, so none is included. If you run one, or your team does, add it here.
recipes.none_yet: No recipes yet. Create one, or browse the registry.
recipes.open_a_session: Open a session to run a recipe.
recipes.risk_none: Nothing risky found. That is not the same as safe.
recipes.understated: The author declared this {{declared}}, but it looks {{actual}}.
recipes.declared_above_scan: Rated {{declared}} by its author. The scan alone found nothing worse; it cannot see through variables.
recipes.opaque: Line {{lines}} downloads and runs code. Nothing here can see what arrives.

marketplace.title: Available Plugins
mcp.confirm_title: An AI wants to run this
mcp.mode_desc: How much you want to be asked. Guards still apply in every mode — a mode only decides whether a human is asked.
mcp.mode_moot: The current agent cannot type, so the mode makes no difference.
mcp.mode_dangerous_hint: Run everything without asking, including commands that destroy data.
mcp.mode_dangerous_active: Dangerous mode is on. Commands run without asking, including ones that destroy data.
mcp.mode_dangerous_confirm: Dangerous mode lets an AI wipe disks, drop databases and take hosts down with no confirmation. Enable it?
mcp.shared_desc: What an AI can read right now. Turn sharing off on a terminal tab, or stop it here.
mcp.shared_none: Nothing is shared. The server is listening, but no session is exposed.
mcp.regenerate_confirm: Replacing the token immediately locks out every client configured with the old one. You will need to re-add the server everywhere. Continue?
mcp.token_regenerated: Token replaced. Every client using the old one is now locked out.
mcp.port_locked: Stop the server to change the port
mcp.mode_ask_hint: Confirm every command before it runs.
mcp.mode_auto_safe_hint: Run read-only commands without asking. Anything that changes the system still asks.
mcp.mode_auto_hint: Run everything without asking, except destructive commands.
mcp.share_tab: Share this session with the AI
mcp.enable_desc: Let an AI client read and type into sessions you share. Off by default; nothing listens until you turn it on.
mcp.port_desc: 0 lets the system pick a free port.
mcp.token_hint: Stored encrypted in your vault and reused across restarts, so a client configured once keeps working. Regenerate to lock out anything using the old one.
mcp.listening_nothing_shared: Listening. No session is shared yet — turn sharing on for a terminal tab.
mcp.agent_desc: The agent decides which tools the AI gets, not just how it behaves. A read-only agent has no way to type.
mcp.connect_desc: Pick your tool and paste this. Every client spells it differently.
mcp.unverified: This syntax is not in the vendor's own documentation — check it connects.
mcp.confirm_notice: Nothing runs unless you approve it. Closing this window rejects the command.

session.import_no_hosts: No hosts found in SSH config
session.rdp_import_desc: Paste a Termix export, or a JSON array of RDP hosts. Each one is added as an RDP session in the selected vault; passwords are never imported — RDP asks for them on connect.
session.rdp_import_filter: Filter by name, host, or folder
session.rdp_import_none: No RDP hosts found in the pasted JSON.
session.import_folder_name_needed: Give the new folder a name
session.delete_n_message: These sessions and their saved settings are removed from every device this vault syncs to. Folders stay.
devops.intro: Tools for running and managing infrastructure: automation, infrastructure as code, databases, containers and Kubernetes. Turn on the ones you use; a tool that is off leaves the tab bar and does nothing, and what it saved is kept for when you turn it back on.
devops.tofu_desc: Plan and apply infrastructure as code.
devops.busy: A run is in progress. Turn it off once it finishes.
devops.not_installed: Not installed on this device. Reach can set it up when you open it.
devops.databases_desc: PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQLite, SQL Server and Redis: browse, query, edit and design.
devops.built_in: Built into Reach, nothing to install
devops.new_notice: New in Reach: Databases for PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server, SQLite and Redis. Switch it on in Settings → DevOps, where Ansible and OpenTofu now live too.
db.ai_explain: Ask AI to explain this query
db.ai_optimize: Ask AI how to make this query faster
db.backup_intro: Writes a .sql file that recreates the tables and their rows in an empty database. Extensions, custom types and permissions are not included.
db.cancel_query_confirm: Stop the statement session {{id}} is running? The session stays connected.
db.close_dirty_confirm: This tab has changes that are not saved. Close it anyway?
db.comment_hint: What this table holds, for whoever reads it next
db.confirm_run_intro: Reach held these back because they delete or rewrite more than a normal change. Nothing has run yet.
db.confirm_run_prod: This is a production connection, so every change is checked first. Nothing has run yet.
db.console_hint: Type a Redis command, e.g. INFO memory or HGETALL user:1. Up and down go through earlier commands.
db.delete_connection_confirm: Delete the saved connection “{{name}}”? The database itself is not touched.
db.designer_needs_name: Give the table a name to see its SQL.
db.discard_confirm: Discard the changes you have not saved?
db.editor_placeholder: Write SQL here. Ctrl+Enter runs the statement under the cursor; Ctrl+Shift+Enter runs everything.
db.explain_hint: Show how the database plans to run the statement
db.generated_hint: An expression; leave empty for a normal field
db.host_from_server: Host, as the SSH server sees it
db.keep_going: Keep going after a failed statement
db.kill_session_confirm: End session {{id}} ({{user}})? Its open transaction is rolled back.
db.name: Name
db.no_key_read_only: This table has no primary key, so rows cannot be picked out safely for editing. Edit it with SQL, or give it a key in the designer.
db.password_kept: Saved — leave empty to keep it
db.pick_key: Pick a key to see its value.
db.production_desc: Ask before every change, not only the destructive ones, and tint it red.
db.read_only_desc: Only reads are allowed; Reach refuses anything that would change data.
db.restore_intro: Runs a .sql file against {{db}}, statement by statement.
db.restore_prod_warn: This is a production connection. A restore can overwrite what is there.
db.review_intro: They run together in one transaction: all of them, or none.
db.review_mysql_note: MySQL applies each structure change on its own; if one fails, the ones before it stay.
db.review_tx_note: These run in one transaction: if any fails, nothing changes.
db.route_hint: Reach logs in over SSH and forwards the database port. The host below is where the database is from that server — usually 127.0.0.1.
db.run_hint: Run a query to see its results here.
db.start_hint: Connect to PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQLite, SQL Server or Redis — directly, or through an SSH session you already have.
db.trigger_hint: The full CREATE TRIGGER statement. Changing it drops the old trigger and creates this one.
db.type_not_shown: Values of type {{type}} are not shown here; use the console.

tofu.state_import_address_help: The address to assign to the resource in state (type.name).

tofu.state_move_prompt: Enter new address for this resource:
tofu.state_remove_confirm: Remove this resource from state? The actual infrastructure will not be destroyed.

tofu.backend_none: No backend configured. Select a backend type to store state remotely.
tofu.encryption_desc: Encrypts the state file and saved plans with AES-256-GCM under a key derived from this passphrase (PBKDF2). The passphrase stays in Reach's vault and reaches OpenTofu as an environment variable; the generated HCL only names the variable. An OpenTofu feature (1.7+); Terraform cannot read the result.
tofu.encryption_warning: Lose the passphrase and the state cannot be read by anyone, Reach included. Keep a copy somewhere you trust.

lock.title: Reach is locked
lock.subtitle: Your open sessions keep running. Unlock to use your vault.
lock.wrong_password: That password did not unlock the vault.
lock.unlock_failed: The vault could not be unlocked. Try your master password.
security.auto_lock_desc: Lock Reach after this long without keyboard or mouse use.
security.lock_on_system_lock_desc: Lock Reach when you lock your computer or it goes to sleep.
lock.biometric_failed: {{method}} did not unlock the vault. Try again or use your master password.
security.biometric_desc: Open the vault with {{method}}. Your master password always works too.
security.biometric_needs_password: Set a master password first, so you can still get in if {{method}} is unavailable.
security.biometric_unavailable: {{method}} is not set up on this device.
lock.set_password_hint: Anyone at this computer can open this lock. Set a master password in {{place}} to protect it.
lock.key_failed: The security key did not unlock the vault. Try again or use your master password.
lock.key_touch: Touch your security key when it blinks.
security.keys_desc: Unlock with a FIDO2 key such as a YubiKey. Add a second key as a backup; your master password always works too.
security.keys_needs_password: Set a master password first, so you can still get in without a key.
security.keys_touch_twice: Touch the key when it blinks. It asks twice: once to add Reach, once to seal the vault key.
settings.login_message_desc: Keep the server's welcome message (MOTD, last login, system status) on screen after connecting, as other SSH clients do.
ssh.key_refused_agent: Logged in to {{host}} with a key from your SSH agent: the server refused this session's own key ({{fingerprint}}). The session will fail on devices without that agent, such as a phone. Put the session's public key in the server's authorized_keys, or import the key the server trusts.
ssh.key_refused_password: Logged in to {{host}} with a password: the server refused this session's key ({{fingerprint}}). Put the session's public key in the server's authorized_keys, or import the key the server trusts.
session.try_agent_keys: Also try my SSH agent's keys if this key is refused
session.try_agent_keys_hint: Off by default. Every key offered counts as a failed login on the server, and servers block an address after a few (fail2ban, MaxAuthTries), and each key tells the server who you are. Without it, a refused key says so clearly.
settings.log_mode: Log SSH sessions to a file
settings.log_mode_desc: Off by default. Saves what the server sends, as PuTTY does: printable output drops colour and cursor codes; all output keeps them. Keystrokes are never logged, but anything shown on screen is, so keep logs private.
settings.log_folder_desc: Where log files are saved. Leave empty for the default.
settings.log_name_desc: &H host, &P port, &Y year, &M month, &D day, &T time (HHMMSS).
settings.log_append_desc: When off, a file with the same name is replaced.
settings.log_header_desc: Writes the date and time at the top of each log.
ssh.log_failed: The session log for {{host}} could not be opened ({{message}}). This session is not being logged.
devops.containers_desc: Docker and Podman on your servers through their SSH sessions: Compose stacks, containers, logs, a shell inside, images and volumes.
devops.kubernetes_desc: Kubernetes clusters from a kubeconfig, directly or through an SSH session: workloads, pods, logs, YAML, events and Helm releases.
env.label: What it is for
env.hint: Production is marked in red everywhere, and changes on it ask you to type the name first.
env.read_only_hint: Read-only: you can look, but changes are refused. Turn it off in the host's or cluster's settings.
status.killed: Killed (out of memory or stopped by force)
logs.older_hidden: {{count}} older lines not shown. Download keeps them all.
help.docker_permission_title: You don't have permission to use Docker on this server
help.docker_permission_body: Docker's socket belongs to root and the docker group, and your SSH user is in neither. Rootless Docker runs it as your own user; adding yourself to the docker group works too, but read the warning first.
help.docker_rootless: Safest: rootless Docker, as your user
help.docker_group: Or add your user to the docker group (then log in again)
help.docker_group_warning: Anyone in the docker group can become root on this server (Docker's own documentation says so).
help.podman_socket_body: Reach talks to Podman through its API socket, which is started by systemd for your user. Start it once and it stays on.
help.engine_missing_title: This server doesn't have that engine
help.engine_missing_body: The command wasn't found. Install Docker or Podman on the server, or choose the other engine in the host's settings.
help.read_only_body: Changes are refused here. To make changes, turn Read-only off in its settings.
help.k8s_unauthorized_title: The cluster didn't accept your credentials
help.k8s_unauthorized_body: The kubeconfig's token or certificate was refused, often because it expired. Get a fresh kubeconfig and edit the cluster to replace it.
help.k8s_forbidden_title: Your account isn't allowed to do that
help.k8s_forbidden_body: The cluster's RBAC rules don't give this identity that permission. Ask the cluster's administrator, or use an account that has it.
ctr.this_computer_hint: Docker or Podman running here (Docker Desktop, Podman Desktop or an engine on Linux).
ctr.session_hint: Reach logs in with this saved session and talks to the engine over SSH. Nothing is opened on the network.
ctr.podman_hint: Podman, rootless or root; uses its API service.
ctr.name: Name
ctr.welcome_body: Manage Docker and Podman on your servers from one place, through the SSH sessions you already have.
ctr.welcome_point_ssh: Nothing to open on the network: everything goes through SSH.
ctr.welcome_point_engines: Docker, rootless Docker and Podman, with Compose stacks.
ctr.welcome_point_safe: Mark a host as Production and changes ask first; Read-only refuses them.
ctr.no_stacks: No Compose stacks on this host.
ctr.no_stacks_hint: Stacks appear here when you start a project with docker compose up.
ctr.stacks_hint: Containers that belong to a stack are also shown under Stacks.
ctr.down_message: Its containers and networks are removed. Starting it again recreates them.
ctr.down_note: Volumes are kept, so your data stays.
ctr.shell_needs_running: Start the container to open a shell in it.
logsrc.read_again_hint: Read the files again from the start of the chosen lines
logsrc.none_found: No log files in the usual places. Type a path below.
logsrc.full_path: Give the full path inside the container, starting with /
logsrc.saved_with_host: Saved with the host, on every device.
logsrc.saved_until_close: Remembered until Reach closes; save the host to keep it.
ctr.builtin_network_hint: The engine's own network; it can't be removed.
ctr.production_action_message: This host is marked Production. Anything using it will be interrupted.
ctr.kill_message: It is stopped at once, without a chance to shut down cleanly.
ctr.remove_container_message: It is stopped if it is running, then removed. Its image stays.
ctr.remove_container_note: Named volumes are kept. This can't be undone.
ctr.remove_image_message: It is deleted from this host. It can be pulled again later.
ctr.remove_volume_message: The volume and everything stored in it are deleted.
ctr.remove_volume_note: This deletes data permanently. It can't be undone.
ctr.remove_network_message: Containers still attached to it would lose this network; the engine refuses if any are.
k8s.all_good_detail: Pods running: {{pods}}. No pod or workload needs attention.
k8s.conflict_body: Your edit was not saved because the object changed after you opened it. Copy your edit if you need it, reload the latest version, then re-apply your change.
k8s.context_paste_first: Paste or choose a kubeconfig first
k8s.daemonset_explain: A DaemonSet runs one pod on each matching node, so it has no replica count to scale.
k8s.delete_namespace_note: Everything inside the namespace is deleted with it: workloads, services, config, secrets and volume claims. This cannot be undone.
k8s.delete_node_note: The node is removed from the cluster. Its pods are not moved first; drain the node beforehand if they should keep running elsewhere.
k8s.delete_object_message: This {{kind}} will be deleted from the cluster.
k8s.delete_object_note: This cannot be undone from Reach.
k8s.delete_pod_bare: Nothing manages this pod, so it will not come back.
k8s.delete_pod_message: The pod is stopped and removed.
k8s.delete_pod_owned: Its controller ({{owner}}) will create a new one, so this works as a restart.
k8s.delete_pvc_note: Depending on the storage class, the volume and its data may be deleted too. This cannot be undone.
k8s.delete_workload_message: The workload and the pods it runs will be deleted.
k8s.delete_workload_note: Its pods stop. Volume claims and configuration it uses are kept.
k8s.empty_in_namespace: Nothing here in {{namespace}}. Try All namespaces.
k8s.helm_no_values: No values were set; the chart's defaults apply.
k8s.helm_rollback_message: The release goes from revision {{from}} back to revision {{to}}. Helm records this as a new revision.
k8s.helm_rollback_note: Workloads go back to that revision's settings; data written since then is not rolled back.
k8s.helm_uninstall_message: Helm deletes everything this release installed, and its history.
k8s.helm_uninstall_note: Volume claims created by the chart may be kept or deleted, depending on the chart. This cannot be undone.
k8s.helm_user_values: Values set at install or upgrade
k8s.helm_where_local: Rollback and uninstall run the helm program on this computer, so helm must be installed here.
k8s.helm_where_session: Rollback and uninstall run the helm program on {{session}}, the server this cluster is reached through, so helm must be installed there.
k8s.hint_config: The container could not be created from its settings. Usually a ConfigMap or Secret it refers to is missing; see Events.
k8s.hint_crash: The container starts and then exits, again and again. The Logs tab usually says why.
k8s.hint_evicted: The node ran short of memory or disk and removed this pod. Its controller usually starts a replacement elsewhere.
k8s.hint_image: The image cannot be downloaded. Check the image name and tag, and that the cluster may pull from that registry.
k8s.hint_oom: The container used more memory than its limit and was stopped. Raise the limit or find what uses the memory.
k8s.hint_pending: The pod is waiting for a node. Often there is not enough CPU or memory, or a volume is not ready; Events says which.
k8s.kc_cloud: Their command-line tools write it to ~/.kube/config:
k8s.kubeconfig_hint: Paste the file's contents or choose the file. It is stored encrypted in your vault and only used to reach this cluster.
k8s.kubeconfig_keep: Leave empty to keep the stored kubeconfig
k8s.kubeconfig_keep_hint: The stored kubeconfig is kept unless you paste or choose a new one.
k8s.kubeconfig_too_big: That file is too large to be a kubeconfig.
k8s.needs_attention_detail: Open an item below to see what is wrong and how to fix it.
k8s.no_events: No events. Kubernetes keeps them for about an hour.
k8s.no_events_pod: No recent events for this pod.
k8s.no_pods_workload: No pods are running for it.
k8s.not_scheduled: Not placed on a node yet
k8s.pick_cluster_hint: Choose a cluster above to connect.
k8s.problems_na: Problems only applies to pods, workloads, nodes, events and Helm.
k8s.read_only_desc: Look, don't touch: Reach refuses every change to this cluster.
k8s.read_only_note: Read-only: changes are turned off in this cluster's settings.
k8s.read_only_prod: On by default for production. Turn it off only when you mean to change things.
k8s.remove_cluster_message: Reach forgets this cluster and its stored kubeconfig.
k8s.remove_cluster_note: Nothing on the cluster itself changes.
k8s.restart_message: Every pod is replaced with a fresh one (a rollout restart).
k8s.restart_note: Pods are replaced a few at a time, as the workload's update strategy allows.
k8s.route_hint: Choose a saved SSH session when the API server is only reachable from that server, such as a bastion host or the node itself.
k8s.scale_explain: How many copies of the pod should run.
k8s.scale_zero_message: Every pod of this workload stops; it serves nothing until it is scaled up again.
k8s.scaled_zero_toast: {{name}} scaled to 0. Use Restore to bring back {{n}}.
k8s.secret_overview: A Secret's values are never loaded for the list. The YAML tab shows them only after a warning, hidden until you reveal them.
k8s.secret_warn_body: This Secret holds passwords, keys or tokens. Its values stay hidden until you choose Reveal; make sure nobody can see your screen first.
k8s.welcome_body: Connect Reach to a Kubernetes cluster to see what runs on it and fix what is broken, from your desktop or your phone.
k8s.welcome_point_health: See at a glance which pods and workloads have problems, in plain words.
k8s.welcome_point_helm: Inspect Helm releases and roll back a bad upgrade.
k8s.welcome_point_logs: Follow logs, read events and edit YAML safely.
k8s.welcome_point_safe: Production clusters start read-only, and every risky action asks first.
k8s.where_kubeconfig: Where do I find my kubeconfig?
k8s.yaml_discard: Discard your changes to this YAML?
k8s.yaml_edit_hint: Saved only if nobody changed it since you opened it.
devops.containers_k8s_notice: New in Reach: Containers (Docker, Podman, Compose) and Kubernetes with Helm, through your SSH sessions. Switch them on in Settings → DevOps.
help.k8s_unreachable_body: Its API server didn't answer. Check that the cluster is running and that its address is reachable: from this device, or from the SSH server if the cluster is reached through one.
sshopt.title: SSH options (ssh_config)
sshopt.intro: Settings as you would write them in ~/.ssh/config. Reach applies them to this session, on every device it syncs to.
sshopt.lines_hint: Any ssh_config keyword, e.g. MACs +hmac-sha1. Lines written here win over an imported file, as ssh -o does.
sshopt.reread_missing: There is no Host {{alias}} in ~/.ssh/config any more.
sshopt.approval_hint: These make the connection weaker than Reach's defaults, or run a program on this computer. Nothing here is used until you tick it.
sshopt.not_yet: Kept with the session, not acted on yet
sshopt.session_field: Used as the session's own setting
sshopt.structure: Shapes how the file is read
sshopt.status_overridden: An earlier line already set this
sshopt.other_host_lines: Lines for other hosts, not shown: {{count}}
sshopt.status_inactive: In a block that does not apply to this host
sshopt.status_deprecated: No longer does anything in OpenSSH
sshopt.status_unsupported: OpenSSH itself no longer supports this
sshopt.import_desc: Each host is read the way ssh reads it, with Match, Include and every option. The files are kept with the session, so it connects the same way on every device.
sshopt.file_errors_title: ssh would refuse your config because of these lines:
sshopt.weaker_hint: You allowed these. Untick one to stop using it.
authprompt.title_confirm: Add the key to the SSH agent?
authprompt.host_hint: Asked while logging in to {{host}}. Nothing you type here is saved.
hostkey.dns_match: Matching host key fingerprint found in DNS.
hostkey.dns_nomatch: No matching host key fingerprint found in DNS.
ssh.weak_kex: {{host}} is not using a post-quantum key exchange ({{kex}}): the session could be recorded now and decrypted later. Upgrading the server fixes it.
